subject: Citywide Pay-to-Park Contract Implementation
overview: The council deliberated on the city's new pay-to-park contract terms and reviewed infrastructure and public safety concerns raised during a neighborhood walk in South Medford. Members also approved funding for DPW salaries and discussed the local impact of the proposed Everett casino.

items.title: Distracted Driving Petition
items.summary: Referred a petition regarding distracted driving awareness to the Traffic and Parking Commission and requested a legal opinion on the feasibility of a local hands-free ordinance.

items.title: Parking Enforcement Petition
items.summary: Placed on file a resident's petition calling for uniform parking enforcement and the implementation of meters in business districts.

items.title: Law Account Claim Approval
items.summary: Approved a $4,498.94 expenditure from the law account to settle a claim by State Farm Insurance for a parked vehicle struck by a DPW sander.

items.title: Meeting Accessibility and Transcripts
items.summary: Referred a request for online meeting archives and transcripts to the Rules Committee to evaluate the $20 DVD fee and requested the administration investigate uploading meetings to the city website.

items.title: Street Sweeping Notifications
items.summary: Requested that police use sirens and bullhorns to notify residents of street sweeping operations in advance of towing cars.

items.title: Handicapped Parking in Business Districts
items.summary: Requested that the administration clarify the number of handicapped spots in the new parking plan and hold informational sessions for the public and business owners.

items.title: Pay-to-Park Contract Investigation
items.summary: Referred the city's pay-to-park contract to the Committee of the Whole to address discrepancies regarding spot counts, snow removal responsibilities, and the mayor's proposed amendments.

items.title: South Medford Neighborhood Safety Walk
items.summary: Referred a punch list of infrastructure repairs to departments following a neighborhood walk and established a plan to hold similar public safety walks in all city sections.

items.title: Water and Sewer Enterprise Transfers
items.summary: Approved transfers of $62,500 and $55,500 from the Water and Sewer Enterprise account to fund DPW salaries and referred a specific leak detection request to the department.

items.title: Casino Impacts and Dog Park Audit
items.summary: Discussed potential traffic and crime impacts associated with the Everett casino proposal and requested a financial audit of all funds received for the city dog park.
